newsitem.title: INDIA: S&P rates India's Reliance notes "BB+".
newsitem.headline: S&P rates India's Reliance notes "BB+".

text.p: U.S. rating agency Standard & Poors said on Friday it assigned a "BB+" long-term rating to Indian petrochemical firm Reliance Industries Ltd's proposed issues of unsecured loans totalling $314 million.
S&P said in a statement it had rated two proposed issues -- $100 million unsecured notes maturing 2097, and $214 million unsecured notes maturing 2027 putable 2007.
The statement said: "The rating on the notes reflects the sovereign credit risk of the Republic of India for foreign currency obligations (rated BB+, with a positive outlook)."
S&P said Reliance was expected to maintain adequate credit protection due to its modern, efficient plants, strong domestic market position and willingness to fund aggressive growth.

S&P said that although factors including commissioning risks and the unpredictable nature of future commodity chemical prices existed, these were mitigated by a strong cash flow, an anticipated highly competitive cost position and a strong track record of successfully bringing plants on-stream.
